clue.text: Country supplying lubrication for the speaker

indicators.note: a speaker says the word out loud, so we want something that sounds like the next word

parts.note: grease is a lubricant, so lubrication supplies the word grease

explanation.surface: A nation that exports oil or grease to keep things running smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan nation whose capital is Athens is a country.

clue.text: Willing victim?

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means ready and willing to try something
the animals hunted, the hunter's prey or victim

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: being up for anything, and hunted animals as prey.

clue.text: To lie in effect means something yellow

indicators.note: to effect is to bring about, so the clue's letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lying down in effect suggests some yellowish result.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a yellow plant pigment formed in shoots grown without light, so it is something yellow.

clue.text: Class for pet with personality on line

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet
ego is one's self or personality
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A classification for a pet whose character is displayed online.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or grouping of things sharing features.

clue.text: In the outset, a load of French food

indicators.note: the load is placed inside the letters from the next word

parts.note: read as SET OUT, the letters of set rearranged
a cargo is a load carried by ship or plane

explanation.surface: At the start, a shipment of French cuisine arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outset' is read as 'set' put out of order, giving EST, which holds CARGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails cooked in the French manner are a classic dish of French cuisine.

clue.text: How to cope with the world's growing pains — eventual best model?

definitions.text: How to cope with the world's growing pains — eventual best model?

parts.words: How to cope with the world's growing pains — eventual best model?
parts.note: describes economic growth that the planet can keep up indefinitely, the ideal pattern for progress in the long run

explanation.definitionFit: Growth that meets present needs without exhausting resources is the long-term model for handling the planet's expansion.

clue.text: Smoker wants to get off the bus

definitions.meaning: someone with an unlit cigarette asks for a match or flame
to step down from a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is what a smoker asks for; as one it means to dismount from transport.

clue.text: George's first and second man in a boat in transports

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: Harris is one of the companions in Jerome K Jerome's novel Three Men in a Boat, alongside George

explanation.surface: George and his friend from the boating story are carried away with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Men in a Boat is a comic Victorian novel about J, George and Harris on the Thames; 'transports' is not rapture but vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Gharris are horse-drawn carriages of India, a form of transport.

clue.text: Cobbler to stick as long as it takes

definitions.meaning: the proverb says a cobbler should stick to his last, the foot-shaped mould
persisting right up to the very end

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means continuing until the final moment, and also completes the proverb about a cobbler and his last.

clue.text: Half of me yet confused

parts.note: moi is French for me

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: A muddled half of myself.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is a half share or one of two parts.

clue.text: Like a hellfire sermon given by a candidate?

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a pious rant: PI is the crossword abbreviation for pious, and a rant is a fiery tirade

explanation.surface: An election hopeful delivering fire-and-brimstone preaching.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone seeking a position, a candidate or hopeful.

clue.text: Forges ahead with old revolutionary to fight for lost cause

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pushes forward with an ageing rebel to battle on for a hopeless cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means wasting effort on something already beyond saving.

clue.text: See 5
Dispute French story about a bird?

indicators.note: the story goes around the bird

parts.note: conte is French for a tale or short story
a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a French tale is really about a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene is to go against or dispute something, such as a rule or claim.

clue.text: Coloured companion for travellers on half ticket

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour
Roma are travelling people

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A fellow journeyer travelling on a half-price fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromatic means relating to or having colour.

clue.text: Traitor causing disturbance at old Caerleon

parts.note: Isca was the Roman name of Caerleon, a town in south Wales
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A turncoat stirring up trouble in an old Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas, the disciple who betrayed Jesus, is the archetypal traitor.

clue.text: Father, a wise old Greek, catches cold

indicators.note: one piece takes in or holds the other

parts.note: Nestor is the wise elder counsellor of Homer's Iliad
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A paternal sage from ancient Greece comes down with a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A forefather, someone from whom one descends, is an ancestor.

clue.text: See 14
City of gold is like Pisa's tower

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
the famous tower in Pisa tilts, so it leans

explanation.surface: A golden city that tilts like the famous Italian tower.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a city on the Loire in France, and also gives its name to New Orleans.

clue.text: Irresponsible fellow's tip to avoid turbulence?

definitions.meaning: a shifty, unreliable person who may vanish overnight
advice to travel by air after dark when the air is calmer

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names an untrustworthy person; read literally it is advice on when to take a flight.

clue.text: Good heavens! One week and I was on a wild goose chase

definitions.text: I was on a wild goose chase

parts.note: gosh is an exclamation of surprise like good heavens
a is one

explanation.surface: A bird recounts a week spent fruitlessly chasing geese.
explanation.walkthrough: A wild goose chase is a futile errand, but here the hawk, whose name means goose-hawk, literally hunts geese.
explanation.definitionFit: This large hawk's name comes from goose hawk, a bird that once hunted wild geese.

clue.text: Play starts with nail polish remover, which is pointless

indicators.note: a point here is a compass point, so one such letter is dropped

parts.note: acetone is the solvent used to remove nail polish

explanation.surface: A drama opens with nail varnish remover, which seems futile.
explanation.walkthrough: E (east) is a compass point; removing it from ACETONE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A play starts with its opening act, the first section of the drama.

clue.text: Man keeping recipe revised by writers in spite of set purpose

indicators.note: the man holds the other letters within him

parts.note: a man is male

indicators.note: a revised text is changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: A chap holds on to a recipe that authors keep changing, despite deliberate intent.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints PRESENSE, but the legal phrase is malice prepense, meaning premeditated malice; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase means intent to harm planned in advance, that is spite with premeditated purpose.

clue.text: Hide from second family?

parts.note: kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Concealing oneself from a stepfamily or other relations.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its skin.

clue.text: Drier up with bottle top to have 1 pound debt

parts.note: a teat is the rubber top on a baby's feeding bottle
to owe one pound: OWE plus L, the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone mopping up with a baby's bottle while owing a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier up' is one who dries up dishes, not a drying wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth used for drying up washed dishes does the job of a drier-up.

clue.text: Criticise a model piece of sailing

parts.note: the Model T was the famous Ford car, so model gives T
a tack is a leg sailed on one course

explanation.surface: Criticising a model yacht's manoeuvre while sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack someone verbally is to criticise them strongly.

clue.text: Record made by group in class

indicators.note: the group goes inside the class

parts.note: a caste is a social class
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A recording produced by a band within a social class.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a tape on which music or sound is recorded.

clue.text: Bust of Comrade Livingstone?

parts.note: bro, short for brother, is a comrade
Ken Livingstone, left-wing former Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A sculpted head of the socialist politician Ken Livingstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a statue but means broken, as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bust, slang for wrecked, is broken.
